clue.text: Know-all uses old way to contact : Brazilian state

indicators.note: one piece is placed touching the next, so the two are joined side by side

parts.note: wise is an archaic noun for a way or manner, as in 'in no wise'
Acre is a state in western Brazil

explanation.surface: A smug expert relies on an antiquated method to get in touch with a region of Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a person who pretends to know everything, a smart alec or know-it-all.

clue.text: Question whether a flower corolla's a drab colour

parts.note: a question asking whether something holds opens with 'Is ...?'
a bell is the cup-shaped corolla of a flower such as a bluebell

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a flower's petals are a dull shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after corolla is a link ('has'), not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is the name for a greyish-yellow or dun shade, a dull colour.

clue.text: Pedestrian description of Reynard returning home?

definitions.meaning: dull and unimaginative, lacking any lift
Reynard is the fox of fable; a fox heading back is bound for its earth, its burrow

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: a fox on its way home is headed for its den.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earthbound is prosaic and cannot soar, the same idea as pedestrian; it also means heading for one's den.

clue.text: Similarity of new caps in room

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Fresh hats in a room look much alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns the ten letters of CAPS IN ROOM into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparison notes likeness between things, so it can stand for similarity or resemblance.

clue.text: Champion's record son held on river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second
held means the son's letter is kept inside the record

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
the Ouse is a river in England (several share the name)

explanation.surface: A champion's disc includes a boy and sits by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is a verb here, with 's as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to support or champion it.

clue.text: Sound bearing identifying one who succeeds

indicators.note: Sound at the start tells us a word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a person's air is their bearing or manner

explanation.surface: A noise from a compass bearing identifies a successor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' suggests a compass direction but means a person's demeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who succeeds to a title or estate.

clue.text: With which Bartholdi achieved eminence right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is sent off

parts.note: stature is eminence or standing

explanation.surface: The sculptor Bartholdi instantly rose to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Bartholdi was the French sculptor of the Statue of Liberty. 'right away' looks like 'immediately', but it removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartholdi's fame rests on a sculpted figure, the Statue of Liberty in New York harbour.

clue.text: They express no thanks at being housed by an artist

indicators.note: being housed by puts the little word inside the painter's name

parts.note: Ingres was a French painter

explanation.surface: Ungrateful guests stay with a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ingres is the 19th-century French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrates are ungrateful people, who give no thanks.

clue.text: Sort of chair that woman used outside

indicators.note: outside puts the phrase for used around the pronoun

parts.note: a chair is used when it is sat on
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: She sat out on a particular style of chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' means SAT ON, as a chair is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheraton is an 18th-century English furniture style named after Thomas Sheraton, so a chair can be of that sort.

clue.text: Grass shows damage by sheep going to and fro

indicators.note: going to and fro says the whole reads the same in either direction

parts.note: mar means damage
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Grassland shows harm from sheep wandering back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to and fro' notes that the joined pieces read the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse dune grass planted to bind sand.

clue.text: Muscle university official applied to secure rejected painting

indicators.note: to secure means the official's title holds the reversed piece inside

parts.note: a proctor is a disciplinary officer at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: rejected means the word for painting is turned back

parts.note: painting as an activity is art

explanation.surface: A university official, to protect the college, applies muscle to a turned-down picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscle' looks like a verb meaning force, but it is the definition: a muscle that extends a limb. 'rejected' reverses the word for painting before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is a muscle that extends a body part, the opposite of a retractor.

clue.text: Social organisation women expect to be in

definitions.meaning: a society of members who meet for leisure
'in the ...' is British slang for pregnant, so an expectant woman is in one

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the club' means pregnant in British slang, and 'expect' points to 'expecting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a society of members; 'in the club' is slang for pregnant.

clue.text: Indignation of male otolaryngologists among others

indicators.note: among places the doctors inside the word for others

parts.note: the rest are the others
ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine, so male specialists are ENT men

explanation.surface: Male ear, nose and throat doctors show anger among their colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: An otolaryngologist is an ear, nose and throat (ENT) doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is bitter indignation at unfair treatment.

clue.text: Revolting students are inside having a meal

indicators.note: inside puts the unit for are within the students' union

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
eating is having a meal

explanation.surface: Rebellious students are indoors having dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like 'rebelling' but means sickening. 'are' is the metric area unit, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauseating means sickening or disgusting, as revolting does.

clue.text: One has a handy profession at one's fingertips

definitions.text: One has a handy profession at one's fingertips

parts.words: One has a handy profession at one's fingertips
parts.note: read literally: a worker whose trade concerns hands and who works on the tips of clients' fingers

explanation.walkthrough: 'handy' means relating to hands, and 'at one's fingertips' is literal: the work is done on nails.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicurist treats hands and fingernails professionally.

clue.text: One quibbles about heading for some Scottish islands

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: North and South Uist are islands of the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone argues about setting off to some Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like travel but takes the first letter of 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: A casuist reasons with subtle, misleading arguments, one who quibbles.

clue.text: Surpass, for example, Westminster's legal competence

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or surpass it
Westminster is a city in London, so it is one example of a city

explanation.surface: Westminster outdoing others in law-making ability.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Westminster is a link ('is').
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity in law is the legal competence to act, such as making a contract.

clue.text: Devastating game, one requiring common sense

parts.note: RU is rugby union
I is the Roman numeral one
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: A crushing match where one needed practical wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS is British slang for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous means causing ruin, devastating.

clue.text: Be the basis of stress medication finally banished

indicators.note: banished means a letter is thrown out

parts.note: to underline is to stress or emphasise

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word medication

explanation.surface: Stress caused by giving up medication at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banished' removes N, the last letter of 'medication', from UNDERLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To underlie something is to lie at its root, to form its basis.

clue.text: A French naval base said to be up to date

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: Brest is a French naval port in Brittany, so a + Brest

explanation.surface: A French port is said to be current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep abreast of events is to be up to date with them.

clue.text: Fellow in allegory not deserving censure

indicators.note: in places the fellow inside the allegory

parts.note: a parable is a story with a moral, an allegory
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: A character in a moral tale is blameless.
explanation.definitionFit: Pardonable means excusable, so not deserving blame.

clue.text: Money demand a children's writer finally dropped

indicators.note: finally dropped means the writer's surname loses its last letter

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote the Swallows and Amazons children's books

explanation.surface: A children's author is at last turned down for the money he asked.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons; losing its last letter gives RANSOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is money demanded for releasing a captive.

clue.text: Set of rules applied to items for sale in the bar?

definitions.meaning: a system of laws or principles

definitions.text: applied to items for sale in the bar?
definitions.meaning: printed on goods for sale, read as striped bars

explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; it is a bar code.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a body of rules; a bar code is printed on items for sale.

clue.text: Suitable name that is adopted by religious community

indicators.note: adopted by puts the abbreviations inside the community

parts.note: a convent is a community of nuns
ie is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A fitting name, taken on by nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Convenient means suitable or fitting for a purpose.

clue.text: Crocodile here perhaps feeling somewhat upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters read upwards
somewhat means only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: A crocodile probably feeling a bit distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes ELIN from inside 'feeling', and 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is a river known for crocodiles, so it is where one might be found.

clue.text: Water on a Dutchman's beard, for Fabian? It depends

annotationWithheld.why: Water on a Dutchman's beard, for Fabian? It depends: a cryptic definition of a hanging frozen drop, but the role of 'for Fabian' could not be established
annotationWithheld.clue: Water on a Dutchman's beard, for Fabian? It depends

clue.text: Difficulties way back involving foreign currency

indicators.note: involving means the reversed road surrounds the money
back means the street abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
the rouble is Russia's currency

explanation.surface: Problems long ago with overseas money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way back' reads as 'long ago', but 'back' reverses the street abbreviation (giving TS), which then wraps round the Russian money.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubles are problems or difficulties.

clue.text: Why Orpheus went to Hades for Eurydice without a break?

definitions.text: Why Orpheus went to Hades for Eurydice
definitions.meaning: in myth Orpheus went to the underworld to bring back his wife; read as three words this says his purpose

explanation.walkthrough: Split into three words, the answer gives Orpheus's reason for going to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Together can mean continuously, as in days together, without a break.
